fixes.explanation: Paul says he suffers "…for the sake of His body, which is the church." He even tells us what the body is, so nobody has to guess. I appreciate that, because a clearly labeled cookie box saves everybody a lot of guessing. The church is Christ's body.

Equal is a nice word, and Scripture does say, "…you are all one in Christ Jesus." (Galatians 3:28) But in this verse Paul's goal is different. He says it is "…so that we may present everyone perfect in Christ."

Free is a true thing about Christ. Scripture says, "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free." (Galatians 5:1) But the word Paul uses here is different. His goal is "…so that we may present everyone perfect in Christ."

Paul does say he's absent from them in body (Colossians 2:5), so a visit is an understandable guess. But the reason he gives is different: "I say this so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric." Nothing in that line asks for a visit.
Paul says, "…I delight to see your orderly condition and firm faith in Christ." He's absent in body, and he's still delighted by what he sees in them. A firm faith is a good thing to be known for.
